lead.title: TRIMTECH signs a deal worth up to $411M with Biogen for its degraders of toxic brain proteins
lead.deck: The Cambridge biotech, founded in 2023 on Leo James and William McEwan's work on the TRIM21 enzyme, announced on November 16 a research collaboration with a license option: up to $32M in upfront and research milestone payments, up to $411M in total plus royalties, with Biogen able to take an exclusive global license to the resulting degraders (targets and indications undisclosed). Its TRIMTAC and TRIMGLUE small molecules reach the central nervous system and preferentially clear toxic aggregates and oligomers while sparing the normal form of the protein: a major pact for a young company that has raised only $47M in seed funding, though the findings remain preclinical.

milestone.title: Novo Nordisk presents data at ObesityWeek suggesting that amylin and calcitonin receptor activation protects bone during weight loss
milestone.summary: In ovariectomized rats, femur trabecular bone volume was 43% higher on cagrilintide and 40% higher on CagriSema than in weight-matched controls (11%, not significant, on semaglutide alone); in healthy volunteers, cagrilintide and zenagamtide suppressed the bone-resorption marker CTX-I, which NN1213, a selective amylin agonist, did not. In the REDEFINE 1 DXA substudy (252 participants), bone density fell on CagriSema but stayed within the normal range for age and sex at week 68.
milestone.why: Bone and muscle loss is the blind spot of obesity treatments: Novo points to the calcitonin receptor as a protective lever, giving European amylin biotechs a new axis of differentiation. The analyses are exploratory and not designed to assess fracture risk, while the FDA is due to rule on CagriSema in Q4 2026.

brefsEurope.title: Moderna creator Flagship Pioneering commits £100M to a London lab that will build AI-native biotechs
brefsEurope.summary: The group's first company-creation lab outside the US, the Flagship Origination Lab plans to recruit around 50 scientist-entrepreneurs in the UK and work with British universities; Flagship is targeting a further £500M through partnerships, not yet secured. No companies or founding teams have been announced yet: a new source of spin-outs to watch in King's Cross.

brefsEurope.title: AmyriAD acquires AD04, a Phase 2b-ready anti-neuroinflammation candidate for mild Alzheimer's, from ADvantage Therapeutics
brefsEurope.summary: The Amsterdam biotech acquires worldwide rights (IP, clinical data, regulatory assets) to this subcutaneous aluminum hydroxide hydrogel injection, which holds a UK Innovation Passport (ILAP); the signal comes from exploratory post hoc analyses of the 332-patient Phase 2 AFF006 trial, where AD04 served as the control. Financial terms were not disclosed.

brefsEurope.title: Galimedix details at CTAD the SAPHARY Phase 2a trial of its GAL-101 pill against toxic forms of amyloid
brefsEurope.summary: The oral small molecule targets misfolded amyloid-beta monomers to prevent the formation of toxic oligomers and protofibrils; the planned trial (NCT07789873) will test 28 days of treatment against placebo in 100 patients with mild to moderate Alzheimer's, assessing safety, PK/PD and exploratory EEG, biomarker and cognition readouts. An oral alternative to anti-amyloid antibodies, still at the planning stage.

brefsEurope.title: Five years of lecanemab: the antibody born at BioArctic keeps slowing decline in the Clarity AD extension presented at CTAD
brefsEurope.summary: In the 351 patients treated continuously for five years, Eisai and Biogen report a 2.05-point CDR-SB difference versus the ADNI natural-history cohort and a 36% relative reduction in the risk of progressing to the next disease stage; among low-tau patients, 66% showed no decline on CDR-SB. An external, non-randomized comparison, but a durability argument for the asset discovered by the Swedish biotech, which licensed global rights to Eisai in 2007.

brefsEurope.title: LifeGlue, a Tampere University spin-out, raises €705,000 to produce its tissue-culture gel to GMP standards
brefsEurope.summary: Its Glue4Life gel, hyaluronic acid-based rather than animal-derived, acts as a scaffold for growing tissues (brain, liver, nerve); on sale since December 2024, it has 15 paying customers in Europe, the US and Australia. The round brings together Finnish, Estonian and Lithuanian business angels and Innovestor's Angel Cofund, with clinical-trial use as the goal.

brefsEurope.title: Kos Biotechnology Partners and research center FORTH to set up a biotech incubator in Crete
brefsEurope.summary: The New York- and Athens-based investor ($125M under management) signed a memorandum of understanding with the Foundation for Research and Technology-Hellas to host startups from the US, Europe, China and Israel on its Heraklion campus, with access to FORTH's labs and equipment. No amounts were disclosed: a signal of an emerging Greek biotech hub.

brefsIntl.title: Seawolf emerges from stealth with $100M and a Sanofi deal worth up to $1.2B for redosable DNA medicines
brefsIntl.summary: Its TRIDENT platform packages in lipid nanoparticles DNA engineered not to trigger an immune response, able to reach the nucleus and drive protein production for longer than RNA; the Versant-led seed and a Series A include Eli Lilly, CRISPR Therapeutics and Novartis's venture fund. Sanofi is committing across multiple targets, including bleeding disorders.

brefsIntl.title: Lilly buys Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B, its 14th acquisition of the year, for a preclinical antibody against myeloproliferative neoplasms
brefsIntl.summary: Formed in 2025 by J.P. Morgan Asset Management's life sciences venture arm, the startup is developing a biparatopic antibody targeting a cell-surface protein specific to CALR mutation-driven disease (myelofibrosis, essential thrombocythemia). A comparable showing that big pharma is now buying as early as preclinical.

brefsIntl.title: CG Oncology's oncolytic virus cuts the risk of relapse after bladder cancer surgery by 68% in Phase 3
brefsIntl.summary: In the PIVOT-006 trial, in patients with intermediate-risk or high-grade non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, cretostimogene reduced the relative risk of relapse by 68% versus surveillance after 17 months of follow-up, with no severe treatment-related adverse events. The company plans to seek approval in this post-surgery setting.

word.definition: An enzyme that sticks a ubiquitin "tag" onto a specific protein to send it to the cell's shredder, the proteasome: new "degrader" drugs hijack these enzymes to get disease-causing proteins destroyed.

parts.label: E3 ligase
parts.role: the recruiter: it recognizes the protein to be removed and transfers ubiquitin to it; humans have more than 600

parts.label: Ubiquitin
parts.role: the tag: a small protein whose chain signals "destroy me"

parts.label: Proteasome
parts.role: the shredder: it cuts the tagged protein into small pieces

how.t: A degrader molecule (a two-armed PROTAC or a "molecular glue") brings an E3 ligase into contact with a target protein it would not have recognized on its own.
The E3 ligase attaches a ubiquitin chain to the target protein.
The proteasome recognizes the tag and destroys the protein; the degrader is released and can start again.

word.why: Choosing the E3 ligase has become the crux of the field: of more than 600 human ligases, only about ten have been used for targeted degradation, dominated by CRBN and VHL, which limits tissue selectivity and invites resistance. Each newly exploitable ligase opens up otherwise inaccessible targets: TRIM21, which only activates when its substrate is clustered, preferentially clears tau aggregates where a conventional PROTAC fails preclinically, hence the deal worth up to $411M between TRIMTECH and Biogen. VC diligence point: is the ligase present in the target tissue (brain, tumor) and protected by IP?

startups.name: TRIMTECH Therapeutics
startups.use: TRIMTAC and TRIMGLUE degraders built on the E3 ligase TRIM21 to clear toxic aggregates in neurodegenerative diseases; deal worth up to $411M with Biogen (November 2026)

startups.name: Amphista Therapeutics
startups.use: Dundee spin-out: Eclipsys "Targeted Glue" platform recruiting novel E3 ligases; its DCAF16-dependent BRD9 degrader AMX-883 received FDA IND clearance in June 2026 in acute myeloid leukemia

startups.name: Proxygen
startups.use: CeMM spin-off systematically mapping interactions between disease proteins and E3 ligases; two glue degrader programs (p300, CDK12) heading toward candidate nomination
